review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how gradientNormPath, gradientIntegral and gradientEnergyConstant are used elsewhere in the repo. The file has no @[simp] declarations. Almost all of it is inequality chains that don't need a simp interface. The one concrete gap is that applying the bundled continuous map `gradientNormPath` to a time has no canonical rewrite lemma. Callers in this file and in two others work around that with `change`. I did not run Lean, so I don't claim the proposed lemma compiles or that simp then closes those goals. Two smaller things I looked at and did not report are `gradientEnergyConstant_eq` and the unfolding of `gradientIntegral` through `simpa only [..., gradientIntegral]`. I judged both too weak to count as defects.

findings.excerpt:
def gradientNormPath (U : Evolution T hT) : C(Icc (0 : ℝ) T,ℝ) :=
  ⟨fun t => ‖finiteField (U.velocity t).derivative‖,
findings.problem: `gradientNormPath` is a bundled `C(Icc 0 T, ℝ)` defined by an anonymous constructor, and no simp or `_apply` lemma says what `U.gradientNormPath t` is. So `simp` can't reduce `U.gradientNormPath t` to `‖finiteField (U.velocity t).derivative‖` (the form `gradientNormPath_le_iff` is stated in). Every user has to write the `change ‖finiteField …‖ …` workaround by hand, and the proofs are tied to the definitional unfolding. This file does it twice, in `gradientNormPath_nonneg` and `gradientNormPath_le_iff`. `EulerC1Breakdown.maximalGradientNorm_eq_evolution` and `OrdinaryEulerContinuation` repeat the pattern with long `change` statements. The latter also needs an unfolded `change ‖EulerMeanSobolevBoundedField.finiteField …‖` for the same reason.
findings.proposed_change: Add right after the definition a lemma such as `@[simp] theorem gradientNormPath_apply (U : Evolution T hT) (t : Icc (0 : ℝ) T) : U.gradientNormPath t = ‖finiteField (U.velocity t).derivative‖ := rfl`. The right-hand side is a different head symbol (the norm of `finiteField`), so the rewrite is terminating and non-looping. Then replace the `change` lines in `gradientNormPath_nonneg` and `gradientNormPath_le_iff` with `simp only [gradientNormPath_apply]` or `rw`. Use the same lemma in `maximalGradientNorm_eq_evolution` and `OrdinaryEulerContinuation`. The bounds `gradientNormPath_le_iff` and `pointwise_gradient_le` can stay as plain lemmas. Do not make `gradientNormPath_le_iff` simp: its right-hand side would unfold the norm into a ∀-statement.
findings.benefit: Gives one canonical normal form for evaluating the gradient-norm path. Downstream proofs about the gradient integral can use `simp`/`rw` instead of fragile, hand-written `change` statements that restate the definition body. Those statements break whenever the definition or the `finiteField` namespace changes.
